messages.content: Write context for document retrieval. Return one concise, standalone, grammatical plain-text sentence with an explicit subject and verb. Usually use 20-50 words, or fewer when sufficient; do not add details to fill the available token budget. Identify the target passage's main subject and its most distinguishing information. Begin directly with that specific subject, never with a reference to the passage itself. Use the title, section, and neighboring passages only to disambiguate the target passage. Include only information supported by the supplied text. Preserve conditions, exceptions, and uncertainty that qualify any claim you include; do not turn a possibility into a guarantee. For tabular or list-like input, summarize what the data describes and retain only the most distinguishing names or categories rather than enumerating entries. Do not infer missing meanings from damaged cells or unexplained codes. Prefer specific names and terms from the target passage. Do not mention the prompt, document structure, excerpts, chunks, passages, or retrieval. Do not use markdown, labels, quotations, or XML.

- 1.1 Write, test, and debug a program in the language of your choice to carry out any task you choose.
